mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the periods following the sustained increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a weakening supply side, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods following the decline in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strong consumer-driven economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 0.5% MoM AND UNRATE decrease > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a robust labor market, which boosts economic sentiment and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a potential deflationary pressure, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a slowdown in consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates a strong economic expansion, which is expected to lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the periods following the sustained increase in GDPC1.
